title: Since and for: how long
goal: Say how long with have been, since and for
intro: To say how long something has continued up to now, English uses the present perfect (continuous), not the present tense: “I have lived here for five years”, “I have been working here since 2020”. “I am working here since 2020” is one of the most common Indian-English mistakes.

rules.rule: for + a length of time; since + a starting point.
examples: for two hours, for ten years
since Monday, since 2019, since I was a child

rules.rule: Action that continues to now: have/has been + -ing.
examples: She’s been learning guitar since March.

rules.rule: State verbs use have/has + past participle.

examples: How long have you been working here?
How long have you known her?

mistakes.right: I have been working here since 2020.
mistakes.why: Up to now: have been working.

mistakes.right: I have known him since childhood.

mistakes.wrong: I am waiting since two hours.
mistakes.right: I have been waiting for two hours.

mistakes.wrong: How long are you living here?
mistakes.right: How long have you been living here?

ex.y: Up to now, state verb: have known.

ex.q: He ___ for this company for ten years.
ex.y: Up to now: has been working.

ex.q: I am living in Chennai since 2018.
ex.fixed: I have been living in Chennai since 2018.
ex.y: Up to now: have been living.

ex.q: We have been waiting since forty minutes.
ex.fixed: We have been waiting for forty minutes.

ex.q: How long do you know Rahul?
ex.fixed: How long have you known Rahul?
ex.y: Up to now: have you known.

ex.a: I have been working here for six years.

ex.q: Correct this: “I am working in this company since 2019.”
a: I have been working in this company since 2019
I've been working in this company since 2019
I have been working at this company since 2019
ex.y: Up to now: I have been working…since.

talk: Introduce your work or studies: how long you have been doing it, since when you have lived in your city, and how long you have known your best friend.
